content:
reza: heads up: deploybot auto-blocked publish for release-712 due to provenance timestamp skew between signer and registry. publish-check error: attestation timestamp (2026-03-21T08:59:00Z) > manifest timestamp (2026-03-21T08:55:00Z) by 4m -> reject.

deploybot: publish-check FAIL: provenance-timestamp-skew exceeds allowed 2m window. see policies: https://go/policies/provenance-time

ops-automation: this usually happens when build machines NTP was stale during signing. we had a brief NTP drift on the EU runners this morning.

anya: product change window closes in 35m. what's risk of forcing a retag or a manual attestation?

deploybot: policy: only allow manual attestation with explicit reason and `manual-attest:clock-drift` flag; audit will record operator. forcing retag without new attestation will fail attestation-check.

reza: options: (1) re-sign artifact in target account with current clock (manual cosign) and approve (2) rebuild and re-sign (preserves CI provenance) (3) extend allowed skew temporarily (infra policy change, risky).

product: prefer fastest that preserves audit. manual cosign acceptable if documented in release notes.

ops-automation: commands if manual path chosen:
```
# target-account session
cosign sign --key ksm://projects/infra/keys/release-signer gcr.io/redwood/release-712@sha256:fff111222
# record reason in deploybot
deploybot approve --image release-712 --env staging --meta manual-attest:clock-drift,operator:reza
```

anya: i'll stand by to run manual cosign if infra can't fix NTP in 15m.

ops-automation: NTP fixed on EU runners, restarting signer agent now. ETA 6m to re-sign via CI.

deploybot: new attestation detected after CI re-sign -> publish-check PASS. Promotion allowed.

product: rolling canary. release note: "Short publish delay due to clock drift during signing; attestation reissued and deployment completed." approved.

reza: follow-up ticket to add CI check for NTP sync before signing: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/1309
